item.title: Desperation Mounts as Thousands in Indiana Endure 10 Days Without Power
item.description: Floods from powerful thunderstorms devastated Gary, where a third of residents live below the poverty line and full restoration isn’t expected until next week.

item.media:description: Dinky Austin called the utility company for updates while she cooled off with ice outside of her home in Gary this week.

item.title: England’s Ancient Trees Are Dying in the Heat
item.description: Extreme temperatures and drought are adding to the stress on oak trees that have lived for hundreds of years and play a key role in the national imagination.

item.description: Tornadoes appeared in Queens and on Long Island as flooding disrupted traffic on some highways. A tornado was also confirmed in Delaware.

item.title: El Niño Is Back. And Worse Than Ever.
item.description: The recurring climate phenomenon is poised this year to enter a new phase known as a super El Niño, exacerbating the effects of climate change.
item.dc:creator: Michael Barbaro, Chico Harlan, Asthaa Chaturvedi, Stella Tan, Adrienne Hurst, Devon Taylor, Marion Lozano, Diane Wong, Pat McCusker and Chris Wood
item.media:credit: Bay Ismoyo/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Rocks exposed at the bottom of a river in Tangerang, Indonesia, last month. Falling water levels in the region are due in part to El Niño, which has brought a prolonged dry season and led to extreme drought, threatening food security in parts of Indonesia.

item.title: Hurricane Lala Destroyed a Hawaii Cemetery, Setting Off a Hunt for the Dead
item.description: In the hamlet of Naalehu, the floods of Hurricane Lala opened graves. One mother sought desperately for her son.
item.dc:creator: Meghan Miner Murray and Madaleine Rubin
item.media:credit: Meghan Miner Murray
item.media:description: The storm turned the small cemetery into torrents of mud, bearing the detritus of death.

item.title: Residents on Hawaii’s Big Island Look to Help One Another After Hurricane Lala
item.description: In a remote region of the ravaged Big Island, there were community gas runs, donated turkey stuffing, a makeshift emergency broadcast and even a helicopter.
item.dc:creator: Orlando Mayorquín
item.media:credit: Ronit Fahl for The New York Times
item.media:description: Brandy Field, from Ka’u Radio, helps to set up internet access in Ocean View, Hawaii, on Monday after Hurricane Lala. The storm knocked out power to thousands on the Big Island.

item.title: What We Know About Damage From Hurricane Lala in Hawaii
item.description: The storm narrowly missed land, but its outer bands left the Big Island with power outages, road closures and flooded homes. At least three people have died in the storm.
item.dc:creator: Christina Morales and Judson Jones
item.media:credit: Bruce Omori for The New York Times
item.media:description: Damage from the storm in Mountain View on the Big Island of Hawaii.

item.title: American Hiker Dies After Lightning Strike on Mount Etna in Italy
item.description: Rescuers found a 29-year-old man in serious condition on the volcano’s eastern slope on Sunday. He was later pronounced dead at a hospital in Catania.
item.dc:creator: Leo Sands and Josephine de La Bruyère
item.media:credit: Salvatore Allegra/Associated Press
item.media:description: Volcanic activity at Mount Etna as seen from Mareneve near Catania in Italy last week. Italian authorities say a 29-year-old American hiker was killed by lightning while hiking on Europe’s most active volcano.

item.title: Hurricane Lala Cuts Off Hawaii Town With Region’s Only Hospital
item.description: Residents of Pahala were stranded after parts of a key highway collapsed under heavy rain. All roads leading to the town and its hospital, on the southern end of the Big Island, are now blocked.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Regalado

item.media:description: Hawaii Department of Transportation workers inspect road damage caused by Hurricane Lala in Pahala on Sunday.

item.title: Hurricane Lala Batters Hilo, Hawaii, Destroying Homes and Leaving Thousands Without Power

item.title: Indiana Prepares for More Rain After Days of Deadly Storms
item.description: Since last week, hazardous weather has caused seven deaths, forced people from their homes and required some to be rescued by boat. The region was at risk for more flooding on Sunday.

item.media:credit: Michelle Pemberton/USA Today Network, via Reuters
item.media:description: Evacuation efforts in Indianapolis on Saturday.

item.title: Lala Damages Utility Lines in Hawaii, Leaving Thousands Without Power
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala damaged 16 transmission lines and many towers on Hawaii’s Big Island, the state’s main utility said.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn
item.media:credit: Bruce Omori for The New York Times
item.media:description: A crew dealing with a damaged utility pole in Hilo, Hawaii, on Saturday. Hawaiian Electric, the state’s primary electric utility, said its customers faced days without power because of the extent of the damage.

item.media:description: An aerial view of a flooded farm after storms in Haleiwa, Oahu, in March.

item.title: Lala Heads for a State With Older Housing Stock
item.description: Experts warned that many houses on the Big Island weren’t built for hurricane-force wind and rain.
item.dc:creator: Aimee Ortiz
item.media:credit: Allan Baxter/Getty Images
item.media:description: Houses at the water’s edge of the Big Island of Hawaii. The median age of a house on the island is 37 years old, and older homes will be more vulnerable to heavy winds and rain.

item.title: Hawaii Braces for Lala After Earlier Flooding
